newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ 1997/98 surplus seen at $1.5 to $2 bln-Radio NZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ 1997/98 surplus seen at $1.5 to $2 bln-Radio NZ.

text.p: The government's surplus for 1997/98 is expected to be between $1.5 billion and $2 billion, Radio New Zealand reported today.
The Budget is due on June 26 and market expectations prior to this week had been for a surplus of $2.9 billion.
The radio item said a speech this afternoon by Treasurer Winston Peters would indicate a lower surplus for the second time in two days.
On Thursday he told parliament he believed external forecasts did not take sufficient notice of the impact of one-off items cutting into next year's expected surplus.

"Our political staff say Winston Peters is softening the ground for next Thursday's Budget, which is likely to reveal the surplus has fallen to somewhere between $1.5 billion and $2 billion - almost half the March figure," Radio NZ said.
In March the government predicted a $3.3 billion surplus for the 1997/98 year.
Treasury and minsterial officials were not prepared to comment on the speculation about the number, but Peters was due to start speaking at 1.15 p.m. (0115 GMT) in Auckland.
